title: Student identity disclosed by submission contents
description: The student shares directly identifying data with the portal during login and assignment submission, including student id and potentially identifying content inside the work file. This creates an identifiability risk because the act of submission ties the assignment to a specific student.
assumptions: The submission includes a student identifier or other identifying metadata/content.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; exact sub-node may vary by the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Submission events can be linked across sessions or courses in transit metadata
description: Data on this flow includes stable identifiers such as student id, course, and submission timestamp. Even aside from file contents, these attributes can allow records of multiple submissions to be linked to the same student across sessions, assignments, or courses if observed or correlated in transit or in communication metadata.
assumptions: An observer or intermediary can access traffic metadata or payload attributes on the flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node may differ depending on whether the methodology distinguishes payload-based versus metadata-based linkability.

title: Student identifiable from data in transit
description: The transmitted student id, course context, timestamp, and possibly the assignment file itself can identify or single out the student if the flow is observed in transit.
assumptions: The flow is observable by an unauthorized party or insufficiently protected in transit.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement due to limited retrieved tree detail.

title: Portal learns sensitive assignment content beyond what is necessary
description: On receipt, the web app processes and stores the full work file together with student id, course, and timestamp. Assignment files may contain personal opinions, writing style, embedded metadata, or other personal data, creating a disclosure risk if the portal collects or exposes more content than is necessary for submission handling.
assumptions: The portal stores or makes the uploaded file accessible to staff, systems, or logs beyond the minimum needed for grading.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine disclosure risk at the destination, but the exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may vary.

title: Student may be unaware of secondary processing of submission data
description: After receiving the submission, the portal may process the file and associated metadata for purposes not obvious to the student, such as plagiarism detection, analytics, retention, or sharing with other university systems. If this is not made transparent, the student lacks awareness of how their data is used.
assumptions: The portal or connected systems perform additional processing not clearly communicated at submission time.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency is insufficient; exact sub-node may differ by tree version.

title: Submission may be collected or retained without valid consent or appropriate legal basis communication
description: The destination may receive and retain the assignment, student id, course, and timestamp without adequately presenting the applicable legal basis, consent choices where relevant, or privacy notice. This creates a non-compliance risk around lawful processing and transparency obligations.
assumptions: The institution relies on consent or must provide notice/controls that are absent or inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends strongly on jurisdiction and institutional context; included as a conditional risk rather than a certainty.

title: Student may be unable to prove what was submitted and when
description: If the portal does not provide reliable evidence such as a receipt, hash, or immutable timestamp, the student could later be unable to demonstrate that a particular assignment file was submitted at a specific time. This creates a non-repudiation/privacy risk around disputes over submission.
assumptions: The system lacks trustworthy submission receipts or audit evidence accessible to the student.
uncertainty_note: Included because the flow explicitly contains a submission timestamp; exact LINDDUN interpretation of non-repudiation may vary by version.

title: Portal shares identified student data with grading service
description: The portal forwards student id together with course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. This is processing and disclosure of identified data, enabling the recipient to directly associate the request and submission with a specific student.
assumptions: Student id is unique within the institution and is sufficient for the grading service to single out the student.

title: Identifiers are exposed on the flow
description: The data flow carries a unique student identifier and contextual attributes such as course and role. If the flow is observable in transit, these data can identify the student associated with a submission or grading request.
assumptions: The student id is present on the wire or otherwise available to intermediaries/observers handling the flow.

title: Course and role metadata can link student activity across requests
description: Repeated transmission of student id, course, file reference, and requesting role can allow observers or intermediaries to correlate multiple submissions and grading-related actions to the same individual across courses or over time.
assumptions: The same student id or stable file references recur across requests, enabling correlation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement for linkability because the retrieved context did not include a specific Linkability subtree.

title: Portal creates attributable evidence of submission/grading requests
description: By sending student id, course, file reference, and role to the grading service, the portal creates evidence that a particular student or requester initiated a submission or grading-related action. This may later reduce the individual's ability to deny involvement in that action.
assumptions: The receiving service logs or otherwise retains the request with sufficient integrity and attribution.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id may vary; retrieved context covered the threat type but not a specific Nr subtree.

title: Grading service learns student-course participation from incoming requests
description: On receipt of the request, the assignment & grading service can infer that the identified student is associated with a particular course and has engaged in submission or grading activity. This reveals personal information beyond the bare identifier.
assumptions: The service or its operators were not already entitled to or aware of the full student-course-action context.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include a disclosure threat subtree.

title: Secondary use of submission metadata by grading service
description: The grading service receives student id, course, file reference, and role for handling assignments and grading. If it uses these data for additional purposes such as analytics, profiling, or monitoring beyond the original routing/grading purpose, the flow enables an unawareness threat for the student.
assumptions: Students may not be fully informed that the grading service receives and may further use these metadata.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on transparency and purpose-limitation context not fully provided in the flow description; subtree id is best-effort.

title: Transfer may exceed data minimization or purpose limitation expectations
description: The portal sends student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the grading service. If any of these attributes are unnecessary for the specific grading operation, or if the transfer is not adequately justified or communicated, the flow may violate privacy requirements such as data minimization or purpose limitation.
assumptions: Not all transmitted fields are strictly necessary for every request type, or the transfer lacks an appropriate legal/policy basis.
uncertainty_note: Compliance assessment requires organizational and legal context not present here; subtree id is best-effort.

title: Excessive disclosure when storing assignment submission metadata
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for grading or later academic administration, the act of sending them to persistent storage constitutes avoidable disclosure of personal data beyond the minimal set required.
assumptions: Assumes at least some of the stored attributes may be more granular or more directly identifying than necessary for the stated purpose, or that purpose limitation/minimisation has not been established.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is based on best judgement for explicit/minimisation-related disclosure; exact subnode may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Stored assignment records enable linkage across submissions and courses
description: By receiving and storing assignment files together with student id, course, and submission time, the assignment store can support linking multiple submissions to the same student across assignments or courses, enabling reconstruction of activity patterns and academic history.
assumptions: Assumes the store retains records in a way that permits querying or correlating by student identifier and related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is selected by best judgement for linkability through persistent identifiers and metadata.

title: Student identity is directly inferable from stored submission data
description: Because the stored record includes a student id alongside the assignment file and contextual metadata, the destination store holds data that directly identifies the submitting student, making identification straightforward for anyone with access to the store or derived datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is unique or readily resolvable to a natural person within the educational context.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is selected by best judgement for direct identifiability from stored identifiers.

title: Stored submission metadata reveals student behavior and academic activity
description: The combination of assignment content, course, and submission time can reveal personal aspects of a student, such as enrollment, working patterns, lateness, participation, or other behavioral traits. Persisting these data in the assignment store creates a detectability threat because the presence and characteristics of a student's submission become observable.
assumptions: Assumes authorized or unauthorized observers of the store can inspect records or metadata, and that timestamps/course context are retained.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is approximate; detectability here is grounded in observability of submission presence and timing from stored metadata.

title: Storage may exceed the student's expectations or valid consent scope
description: If the student was not adequately informed that the assignment file, student id, course, and precise submission time would be persistently stored for specific purposes and retention periods, the destination's storage and subsequent processing may violate consent or broader transparency/expectation requirements.
assumptions: Assumes consent, notice, or another legal basis/purpose specification may be incomplete, unclear, or narrower than the actual storage practice.
uncertainty_note: This is contingent on governance context not provided in the flow description; included because persistent storage of identifiable educational records commonly raises non-compliance risk when notice/purpose/retention are unclear.

title: Teacher submits identified account credentials and role context
description: When logging in and requesting the review queue, the teacher provides identified data such as username/email and implicitly their teacher role and course affiliation. The act of sharing this identified data creates an identifying threat if more identity information than necessary is sent for this request.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes direct identifiers or stable account identifiers tied to the teacher.

title: Request metadata can link teacher activity across sessions
description: The flow may expose stable identifiers and metadata in transit, such as account identifiers, session identifiers, IP address, timing, and requested course context. These can allow linking multiple review-queue requests to the same teacher over time.
assumptions: Assumes network-visible metadata or application-layer identifiers are present on the flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a more specific linkability node.

title: Login and queue request disclose teacher-course relationship and work activity in transit
description: Even if content is limited, the request can disclose that a specific teacher is active, is associated with certain courses, and is currently reviewing submissions. This reveals personal and behavioral information through the transmitted data and metadata.
assumptions: Assumes the request contains course identifiers or other context indicating what queue is being accessed.
uncertainty_note: Specific disclosure node is based on best judgement because no disclosure tree excerpt was provided in context.

title: Portal may process login/request data without sufficient transparency to the teacher
description: On receipt of the login and queue request, the web app may use the teacher's identifiers, course context, and activity data for purposes not apparent to the teacher, such as analytics, monitoring, or profiling of review behavior. If this processing is not adequately communicated, it creates an unawareness threat.
assumptions: Assumes the portal performs secondary processing or logging beyond what the teacher reasonably expects for authentication and queue retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; no unawareness tree excerpt was provided.

title: Portal may collect or retain request data beyond what is necessary for queue retrieval
description: The destination may process and store more teacher login and request data than needed to authenticate the teacher and return the submission queue, for example excessive logs, detailed activity traces, or unnecessary identifiers. This creates a non-compliance risk with data minimization and purpose-limitation obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the application logs or retains request details beyond strict operational necessity.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-compliance node is based on best judgement because no Nc tree excerpt was provided.

title: Excessive disclosure of student data to teacher
description: The portal may disclose more personal data than necessary when displaying submissions to the teacher, such as full student names, detailed work content, and precise submission times for all students regardless of the teacher's need-to-know. This creates a disclosure risk because the source process chooses the scope and granularity of data shared.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may present broader or more detailed submission information than is strictly necessary for the teacher's task, or may not sufficiently limit visibility to the teacher's own classes.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on whether access control and data minimization are properly enforced in the portal UI; the flow description alone does not confirm over-disclosure.

title: Identifiability of students in transit
description: The data flow contains direct identifiers such as student names alongside submission content and timestamps. Anyone able to observe the transmission could identify individual students from the data in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the transmission could be observed by an unauthorized party, e.g. due to insufficient transport protection or endpoint exposure.
uncertainty_note: If strong transport encryption and secure session handling are in place, this threat is substantially reduced.

title: Linkability of student activities across submissions
description: Combining student names, work content, and submission times in the same flow enables records about the same student to be linked across assignments or sessions. This can reveal patterns of behavior or performance over time.
assumptions: Assumes repeated transmissions of similar data occur and that an observer or recipient can correlate them across events.

title: Disclosure of sensitive submission content in transit
description: Submission work content and timestamps may reveal personal, educational, or behavioral information about students. If intercepted or exposed during transmission, confidential student information could be disclosed.

uncertainty_note: Likelihood depends strongly on transport security, browser caching controls, and intermediary logging practices.

title: Unauthorized further disclosure by teacher
description: Once the teacher receives student names, work content, and submission times, the teacher could further share, copy, or retain this information beyond the intended educational purpose, causing a privacy disclosure at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher may have means to export, screenshot, copy, or otherwise redistribute the displayed information.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine destination-side privacy risk, but actual likelihood depends on organizational policy, training, and technical controls.

title: Unawareness of teacher-side handling of student data
description: Students may be unaware of how their submissions, names, and timestamps are viewed, retained, or further used by the teacher after display. This creates an unawareness threat at the destination because the recipient's handling may not be transparent to the students.
assumptions: Assumes students are not clearly informed about teacher access, retention, and onward use of submission data.

If the submission is not strongly bound to the teacher's authenticated identity, timestamped, and integrity-protected, the teacher could plausibly deny having entered or changed the grade or feedback, creating a privacy-relevant accountability gap around personal data processing.
assumptions: Applies if the portal lacks reliable audit logging, strong authentication/session binding, or tamper-evident submission records.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id is best-judgement; exact subnode may differ in the project's LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Teacher and student may be identifiable from grade-submission data in transit
description: The flow carries direct identifiers such as student id and grader id, and may also expose network metadata. If transmission is observable, these data can identify the teacher and student associated with a specific grading event.

uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement at category level; linkage risk is strongly supported by the data fields.

description: The flow contains a student's grade and written feedback, which are personal and potentially sensitive educational records. Interception or exposure of the payload during transmission would disclose private information about the student and the teacher's assessment.

title: Portal may process grading data beyond the teacher's or institution's expected purpose

Such secondary use would make the processing purpose insufficiently transparent or incompatible with the original context.
